percent-base.title: Percentages and the quantity they apply to

examples.input: Buy for $80k; repair for $50k; value increases by 150%. Profit?
examples.why: An increase of 150% includes the original value.

examples.wrong: Solve backwards from a $40 final bill.

percent-base.symptom: The model sometimes applies a percentage to the wrong quantity or confuses an increase with the final value.

time-rate.title: Time, rates, and repeated schedules [lead: fresh baseline needed]

examples.input: 60 miles over 3 hours, then 1.5 hours on each of two days. Speed?
examples.wrong: Compute 12 miles and divide by 6 hours.
examples.why: The stated distance must be preserved.

examples.input: Three 1-hour classes on three days; two 2-hour classes on two days; 16 weeks.
examples.why: The second schedule needs both class count and class duration.

time-rate.symptom: The model sometimes mixes units, drops a time interval, or miscounts a repeated schedule.

group-count.title: Groups, per-item quantities, and multiplicity [lead: fresh baseline needed]

examples.input: Four schools each send two five-player teams and one coach per team.
examples.why: Teams are groups, not individual people.

examples.input: 13 toy sets; sell some at $15 each, buy 8 games at $20, keep $5. Sets left?
examples.wrong: Assume all 13 sets were sold: zero remain.
examples.why: Infer the number sold from the spending and remainder.

group-count.symptom: The model sometimes counts groups instead of their members or applies a multiplier twice.
